paragraphs.text: The lesson keeps filling the day. Page 44 ended with lunch; the next photograph is a table with a cake on it, and the heading tells you when it happens: {{de:Kaffee und Kuchen}}. In German speaking countries this is a fixed appointment in the afternoon, not a stray snack — an invitation to it is an invitation to sit down for half an hour.
Kaffee und Kuchen: der Kaffee · der Kuchen · die Sahne · die Schokolade · der Keks · der Zucker

The second photograph is supper, and it is deliberately plain: bread, something on the bread, a bowl of soup, a salad. Learn these seven words as one scene rather than as seven items — {{de:Abendessen}} is the meal where most of them actually appear in life.
Abendessen: die Butter · das Brot · die Tomate · die Gurke · der Salat · die Suppe · die Wurst · der Schinken

Exercise 2b sends you back to the audio with a list of twelve checkboxes, and exercise 2c asks the question that turns vocabulary into a sentence: where do you buy it? The model is printed in the corner — {{de:Ich kaufe Brot in der Bäckerei}}. Four shops, four prepositions: {{de:in der Bäckerei}}, {{de:auf dem Markt}}, {{de:in der Metzgerei}}, {{de:im Supermarkt}}. The preposition comes from the place, not from the food, so it stays the same whatever you buy.

blocks.prompt: Fill the gap with the right shop. Use the model sentence.

items.hint: der Laden für Brot und Brötchen
der Laden für Fleisch und Wurst
der Platz für Gemüse und Obst
